claim: Urban fire activity can vary with climatic warming
evidence: Shi et al. 2025; Yao et al. 2024
boundary: Prior studies concern broader urban or building-fire series, not this event database

claim: The database contains 239 documented events in 52 countries or regions
boundary: Documented events are not a census of global fire incidence

claim: The core cohort contains 191 traceable non-external events
boundary: Source grade is an operational reproducibility criterion

claim: The primary ERA5-Land analysis does not support a positive association between the heatwave indicator and a documented event day
boundary: OR 0.72; 95% CI 0.24-2.18; P=0.563; 21 informative strata; imprecision does not prove no effect

claim: The exploratory heat score is not clearly associated with reported total-casualty severity
boundary: RR 1.04 per 10 points; 95% CI 0.90-1.21; P=0.608; 66 events with both deaths and injuries reported; selective reporting remains

claim: Population and built volume indicate exposed urban fabric rather than causal ignition mechanisms
boundary: Static 2018/2020 layers are temporally mismatched to some events

claim: Resource planning should consider risk and equity
boundary: Evidence is United States-specific

claim: Heatwaves are at least three consecutive locally extreme days
boundary: Primary threshold is P90 plus a 30 degrees C floor; alternative definitions are sensitivity analyses

claim: High-rise evacuation choices depend on route visibility and building configuration
boundary: One 35-floor hotel experiment with 67 participants; not a universal behavioural law

claim: Façade suppression configuration can alter upward flame migration and heat flux
boundary: Large-scale controlled façade experiments; not direct evidence about ambient heatwaves

claim: Population density and land use can explain local spatial concentration of recorded urban fires
boundary: One district in China; supports contextual modelling rather than global generalisation

claim: GHSL built volume provides gridded surrounding built-form context
boundary: Static gridded context is not incident-building geometry

claim: Numeric injury reporting increases with country-year GDP and decreases for grade-C sources
boundary: Exploratory association in 221 documented extended-cohort events; not an injury-risk model

claim: Numeric evacuation reporting increases with event year and decreases for grade-C sources
boundary: Exploratory association in 221 documented extended-cohort events; not an evacuation-risk model

claim: NASA POWER heatwave estimates are directionally positive but imprecise across prespecified definitions
evidence: Conditional logistic sensitivity models and Supplementary Figure S2
boundary: Independent coarse-grid local-solar-time product; 7--43 informative strata; all confidence intervals include one; not the primary ERA5-Land estimate

claim: Reported deaths and injuries are highly concentrated across documented extended-cohort events
boundary: Gini coefficients describe available numeric records and not population incidence or all missing consequences

claim: Recorded consequence magnitude varies with year GDP and event type after measured adjustment
evidence: Reporting-weighted log-linear exploratory models and Supplementary Table S8
boundary: Conditional on documentation and available building size; no multiplicity adjustment; lower ratios must not be interpreted as protective causal effects

claim: Available national fire-service capacity estimates are imprecise across recorded consequence models
evidence: CTIF Table 1.13 sensitivity models and Supplementary Figure S4
boundary: Cross-sectional most-recent values during 2010-2023; partial country coverage; all confidence intervals include one; neither causal evidence nor evidence of no effect

claim: Independent-product heat estimates are directionally sensitive and imprecise across evidence and geographic restrictions
evidence: NASA POWER cohort exclusion and leave-one-continent-out models and Supplementary Figure S5
boundary: All 12 models converged and all confidence intervals include one; only 9-17 informative strata; this does not replace the ERA5-Land primary analysis

claim: Documentation and consequence missingness in global event databases can be structured by time country context event attributes and media attention
evidence: Jones et al. 2022 and Fetzer and Garg 2026
boundary: Direct evidence comes from global natural-disaster databases and cross-border disaster news rather than a global fire registry; used as design motivation only

claim: Urban fire severity prediction can connect building temporal and GIS features to resource-allocation scenarios
boundary: One-city predictive and simulation study; supports operational context but not cross-national capacity effectiveness or causal impact

claim: Authenticated Earth Engine extraction covers every valid event coordinate and every ERA5-Land matched-day stratum
boundary: 233 valid coordinates completed; 995 matched days in 228 strata; five strata used a documented 20-km coastal fallback

claim: Weather-product choice changes the direction of the primary heatwave point estimate
evidence: ERA5-Land and NASA POWER conditional logistic models
boundary: ERA5-Land OR 0.72 and NASA POWER OR 1.14; both intervals include one; disagreement is exposure-product sensitivity rather than evidence for either sign
